provenance.what: Wire-format probe of Microsoft-Decision-1 on the operator's Foundry resource (docs/features/decision-1-d6-evaluation/plan.md, Task 2). Synthetic content only.
provenance.consent: Operator, 2026-10-16: at most 8 requests, synthetic content only, under $0.001.
provenance.documentation: Microsoft Learn, "Deploy and use Microsoft-Decision-1 in Microsoft Foundry", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/how-to/use-foundry-models-microsoft-decision (ms.date 2026-10-07, updated_at 2026-10-09, git_commit_id 414c6c21ba6c7fda91deaf6ea3699069db91afe6), read 2026-10-16. It gives the request body {model, state, questions}, a choice question as {type, instructions, criteria}, the api-key header for an API key, and Authorization: Bearer for an Entra ID token.
provenance.earlierAttempt: A first run the same day used a malformed stored key. 3 requests using it failed inside Node's fetch with "TypeError: fetch failed" in 0-20 ms and received no response; the invalid-key request reached the resource and returned 401. That run's records are not kept. It and this run together made 8 attempts, 5 of which reached the resource.
observed: The response's model is "microsoft-decision-1", the underlying model, not the deployment name, and carries no version.
A choice answer has exactly the fields choice, confidence, probabilities and type; probabilities has one entry per criteria option.
An unknown deployment returns 404 with error code DeploymentNotFound, not the 422 the documentation's troubleshooting table lists.
provenance.costEstimate: 1079 input tokens at $0.042 per million: $0.0000453. The error responses report no usage.
provenance.dropped: The API key (each record says whether the configured key or a literal was sent). Every response header except those whose name contains request-id. Nothing else.
